guidelines.fragment_description: A Use Case represents a functionality or service provided by the system. It is a primary construct that can stand alone but is often connected to Actors or other Use Cases.
An Actor represents a role played by an external entity that interacts with the system. It is a primary construct that can also stand alone but is typically linked to Use Cases.
An Association relationship between an Actor and a Use Case, showing that the Actor interacts with or participates in the Use Case.
An Include relationship indicates that a Use Case explicitly incorporates the behavior of another Use Case.
An Extend relationship indicates that the behavior of a Use Case can be optionally extended by the behavior of another Use Case.
A Generalization relationship between two Actors, where one Actor inherits the role and responsibilities of another Actor.
A Generalization relationship between Use Cases, indicating that one Use Case is a special type of another Use Case.

guidelines.fragment_description: An actor represents a role that interacts with the use case within the system.
A use case represents a functional requirement of the system, defining interactions between an actor and the system.
An association between an actor and a use case demonstrates that the actor participates in the use case.
An include relationship between two use cases indicates that behavior of the included use case is inserted into the base use case.
An extend relationship implies that the behavior of the extending use case can be inserted into the base use case under certain conditions.
A generalization relationship between use cases where the child use case inherits the behavior and meaning of the parent use case.
A generalization relationship between actors where the child actor role inherits the behavior and responsibility of the parent actor role.
A system boundary defines the scope of the system for the use case under consideration.

guidelines.fragment_description: Represents an entity that interacts with the system in the Use Case Diagram. Typically depicted by a stick figure or a rectangle.
Defines the functionalities or services provided by the system as seen by the actors.
An association relationship connects an actor to a use case, indicating that the actor participates in the use case.
The 'include' relationship is used to include the behavior of another use case into the base use case, indicating that the included use case occurs every time the base use case does.
The 'extend' relationship specifies that the behavior of a use case can be extended by another use case under certain conditions, adding optional behavior.
Represents the boundary of the system, encapsulating use cases and demarcating them from actors outside the boundary.

clusters.canonical_description: Actors represent roles or entities that interact with the system.
Use Cases represent functionalities or services provided by the system and define interactions between actors and the system.
Generalization relationship between actors indicates that one actor inherits roles and responsibilities from another.
Generalization relationship between use cases indicates inheritance of behavior between use cases.
The include relationship shows that one use case incorporates the behavior of another use case.
The extend relationship indicates that the behavior of a use case can be optionally extended by another use case.
An association relationship between actors and use cases shows participation in the use case.
System boundaries define the scope of the system, encapsulating use cases and distinguishing them from external actors.
